topic: Groe Solutions Appoints Julio Marshall as Chief Commercial Officer

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Groe Solutions Appoints Julio Marshall as Chief Commercial Officer

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Groe Solutions announced that Julio Marshall has joined the company as chief commercial officer. Marshall will lead commercial strategy, enterprise sales, revenue operations and strategic partnerships while helping align company operations around Groe’s next stage of growth. Multi-location health club operators often manage member, facility and operating insights across disconnected systems. GroeFit develops smart facilities through computer vision technology and MMS integrations to bring member activity, facility demand and operational signals into the same operating picture. By getting a full understanding of member behavior in relation to the club; highlighting a few of the features, GroeFit helps staff deliver hyper-personalized member communication, provides gym space and equipment intelligence, analyzes and tracks group fitness classes, monitors tailgating and builds unique behavioral patterns of loyal to non-loyal members. Marshall’s appointment strengthens Groe’s ability to connect this gym intelligence platform to the leading decision makers of the industry. “Julio understands that durable growth in fitness is built on trust, disciplined execution and a clear view of what operators need,” said Alantheus Thompso n, the CEO Groe. “He has spent his career listening to club owners, understanding the pressures they face and building relationships that last.

topic: Andrew Huberman Joins Hims & Hers Board

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Andrew Huberman Joins Hims & Hers Board

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Lab partners. Huberman is joining Hims as a non-independent board member, guiding science and marketing. Terms. Per an SEC filing, the deal could bank Huberman up to $24M plus board comp ($50K cash + $250K equity annually). That includes $7M for two years of advisory, $15M to Scicomm Media for three years of podcast ads, and up to $1M annually for optional short-form videos. Underperforming by Wall Street’s standards, Hims’ revenue rose 49% YoY in Q3, but it reported a net loss of $33M, sending its stock and 2026 forecast down. Logic. Aligning with Hims CEO Andrew Dudum’s goal of democratizing personalized healthcare for “the middle 95%,” Huberman initiated the relationship — with Hims’ ownership of end-to-end, US-based peptide manufacturing a major selling point. The platform is prepping the rollout of sermorelin, glutathione, B12, NAD+, and L-carnitine, with BPC-157 and TB-500 to follow when allowed. Strategy. Stoking agency to distinguish from Big Pharma, DTC health ads veer unhinged , with peptide sellers using pointed vibes to woo consumers. Focused on GLP-1s, Ro signed Charles Barkley and Serena Williams as ambassadors, using their athletic history to challenge stigma. Takeaway: Making marketing ubiquitous, companies want to normalize peptides as an entry point to next-gen care — steering messaging away from biohacking and toward basic health .

en.headline: Andrew Huberman Joins Hims & Hers Board

topic: How AXLE Took the the Guesswork Out of JETSET Pilates Franchisee Marketing

facts.label: Story
facts.value: How AXLE Took the the Guesswork Out of JETSET Pilates Franchisee Marketing

facts.label: Article
facts.value: With hundreds of franchisees to support, JETSET Pilates is leveraging AXLE to balance marketing consistency with the flexibility owners need to succeed At JETSET Pilates, every movement requires precision, a certain level of control and purpose. Now with a growing franchise network branching out behind it, the brand knows it needs a similar, equally-responsible approach to marketing. And, just like someone on a reformer, it knows it can benefit from having an instructor or teammate watching over them and assisting when needed. For JETSET , that was AXLE , a technology platform that offers tailored solutions for businesses in the fitness, wellness and beauty industries. Thus far, it’s helped JETSET manage its 150+ locations, giving the right amount of support to empower them without infringing on the responsibilities best left in their hands. Franchisees Face a Challenge Every brand wants to expand and grow its footprint, but doing so doesn’t come without challenges. From a marketing perspective, more sites means requiring more owners to interpret how campaigns should be run or assets utilized. With that, the opportunity for misalignment across the network grows.
